result.note: Tests the Paris Agreement article behind the India–Japan JCM, plus the ITMO credits and the institutional mechanics added by the June 2026 Rules of Implementation.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, India and Japan adopted the Rules of Implementation for their Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM). Under which provision of the Paris Agreement does Japan fund low-carbon projects in India through the JCM?
questions.explain: The JCM operates under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement. Japan funds low-carbon projects in India and counts a share of the verified reductions toward its own climate targets.
questions.source: Under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, Japan funds low-carbon projects in India.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM), whose Rules of Implementation were adopted in June 2026:
items: The JCM is a crediting scheme run by India that pays for emission cuts in Japan.
Verified emission reductions under it are converted into carbon credits known as Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs).
The Rules of Implementation provide for a Joint Committee, registry systems and anti-double-counting rules.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the JCM is a Japanese-run scheme in which Japan funds low-carbon projects in India. The Rules of Implementation adopted on 8 June 2026 add the mechanics to the Memorandum of Cooperation signed in 2025.
questions.source: The resulting emission reductions are verified and converted into carbon credits known as Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs).
